title: The Empty House of Banu Jahsh • ‘Ayyash’s Mother’s Oath • Waiting for Permission • The Night Council of Quraysh • The Visitor at Noon • The Bed of That Night • The Waistband of Asma’ • The Cave of Thawr • The Rock at Noon

blocks.0: The Empty House of Banu Jahsh
blocks.1: One day in a neighbourhood of Makkah an entire house became empty. ‘Abdullah ibn Jahsh (RA) had gone with everyone of the household; his wife, his brothers, his sisters, women and men, all. Not a lock on the door; there was simply no one in the house. ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah, ‘Abbas and Abu Jahl were passing by. ‘Utbah saw the doors of Banu Jahsh rattling in the wind. No one inside. He sighed. He said, every house, however long its happiness, one day calamity and misfortune seize it. The house of Banu Jahsh lies today without its people. Abu Jahl said, are you weeping for so-and-so’s son? Then he said to ‘Abbas, this is the work of your nephew. He has split our community, torn our affairs apart, caused separation among us.{{1}}
blocks.3: ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) himself told how their Hijrah happened. Three decided: ‘Umar (RA), ‘Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi‘ah (RA) and Hisham ibn al-‘As (RA). They would meet at dawn at a place called Tanadib outside Makkah. Whoever did not reach there, it would be understood that he had been held back; the other two would go on. ‘Umar (RA) and ‘Ayyash (RA) arrived. Hisham was held back; he fell into trial. Reaching Madinah they stayed at Quba. After some days Abu Jahl and his brother al-Harith came from Makkah. ‘Ayyash (RA) was their cousin, and on the mother’s side also a brother.
blocks.4: They said to ‘Ayyash (RA), your mother has vowed that no comb will touch her head until she sees you, and that she will not go from the sun into shade. ‘Ayyash’s (RA) heart softened. I said, by Allah, these people want to turn you away from your din; beware. If lice trouble your mother she will comb for herself; if the heat of Makkah grows she will go into shade.{{1}}
blocks.5: ‘Ayyash (RA) said, let me fulfil my mother’s oath. I also have some wealth in Makkah; I will bring it. ‘Umar (RA) said, I am one of the richest of Quraysh. Take half my wealth, do not go with them. ‘Ayyash (RA) did not listen. Then ‘Umar (RA) said, if you will go anyway, take this she-camel of mine. The she-camel is clever, fast. If you suspect anything of their intentions, flee on her back. After going some distance Abu Jahl said, brother, my camel is giving me much trouble. Will you let me ride a little on this she-camel of yours? ‘Ayyash (RA) said, of course. He made the camel kneel. He got down. As soon as the foot touched the ground, the two pounced and bound him. They brought him into Makkah and put him into trial. The mother’s oath was a ruse to bring the son back.
blocks.7: But the Prophet {{1}} did not go.
blocks.9: Abu Bakr (RA) prepared to go toward Madinah. The Messenger of Allah {{1}} said to him, take it slowly; I hope I too will be given permission. Abu Bakr (RA) said, may my father be your ransom, do you hope for that? He said, yes. Then Abu Bakr (RA) held himself back to be a companion of the Messenger of Allah {{2}}, and fed two mounts he had, for four months, the leaves of the samur tree.{{3}}
blocks.10: Four months. One man looking after two camels, only waiting for a single day. At ‘Aqabah Madinah had called him. But until the word ‘go’ came from Allah’s side, he did not lift his foot.
blocks.12: Meanwhile in Makkah Quraysh had sensed it. Islam was spreading fast. Many people in Madinah had believed. The companions of the Prophet {{1}} were leaving one by one.{{2}}
blocks.13: So they sat in consultation. The Qur’an itself tells of that night.
blocks.15: (O Prophet!) Remember the time when the disbelievers were plotting to imprison you or to kill you or to expel you (from the land). They were scheming, and Allah was also employing His plan. In truth, Allah is the best of planners.{{1}}
blocks.16: A little more detail of that night has been given by Ibn ‘Abbas (RA).
blocks.18: Quraysh consulted one night in Makkah. One of them said, when it is morning, bind him; they meant the Prophet {{1}}. Another said, rather kill him. Another said, rather expel him. Then Allah informed His Prophet of it.{{2}}
blocks.19: But the last sentence of the verse says whose hand holds the last move. What happened inside the council, Ibn Ishaq has told from Ibn ‘Abbas (RA). Dar al-Nadwah; that house of Qusayy ibn Kilab, where Quraysh never rose without taking some great decision. At the door an old man. In a thick cloak. He said, I am a shaykh of Najd. I have heard what you have gathered about. My counsel may be of use. He was allowed in. In the narration, this shaykh was Iblis.{{1}}
blocks.20: In the council were ‘Utbah and Shaybah, Abu Sufyan, Jubayr ibn Mut‘im, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Abu al-Bakhtari, Hakim ibn Hizam, Abu Jahl, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and many others. One said, bind him in chains and keep him imprisoned in a house. He will die just as the poets before him died. The shaykh of Najd said, no. His word will surely get out from beyond this door. His companions will come and snatch him away. Another said, expel him from the city. The shaykh said, no. Have you not seen his sweet speech? He will go to any tribe of the Arabs, conquer them, and come back; what then? Then Abu Jahl said, I have an opinion that has not come to your minds. From every tribe one young man, spirited, of good lineage. In each one’s hand a sharp sword. All at once, one blow. Then his blood will be divided over all the tribes. Banu ‘Abd Manaf will not be able to fight everyone; they will agree to take blood-money, and we will pay it. The shaykh of Najd said, this man’s opinion is right. There is no other view than this. The council broke up.
blocks.22: That day ‘A’ishah (RA) was at home. Later she herself narrated it. Every day the Prophet {{1}} would come to the house of Abu Bakr (RA); once in the morning, once in the evening.{{2}}
blocks.23: That day he came at noon.
blocks.25: One day we were sitting in the house of Abu Bakr (RA), at the harsh time of noon. Someone said to Abu Bakr (RA), here is the Messenger of Allah {{1}}, coming with his head covered; at a time when he did not come to us. Abu Bakr (RA) said, may my father and mother be his ransom; by Allah, at this hour he must have come on some great matter.{{2}}
blocks.26: What the Prophet {{1}} said on entering reached the ears of ‘A’ishah (RA).
blocks.28: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} came, asked permission; permission was given, he entered. He said to Abu Bakr (RA), send out those who are with you. Abu Bakr (RA) said, they are only your family, may my father be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah. He said, I have been given permission to leave. Abu Bakr (RA) said, companionship? May my father be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah! The Messenger of Allah {{2}} said, yes. Abu Bakr (RA) said, then take one of these two mounts of mine, may my father be your ransom. The Messenger of Allah {{3}} said, for the price.{{4}}
blocks.29: ‘Companionship?’ One word. And an answer in one word, ‘Yes.’ Four months of waiting ended in one word.
blocks.31: The night of departure. The youths of Quraysh have surrounded the house of the Prophet {{1}}. The plan: in the morning all together to pounce.
blocks.33: That night ‘Ali (RA) spent the night in the bed of the Prophet {{1}}, and the Prophet {{2}} went out and reached the cave. The polytheists guarded ‘Ali (RA), thinking him the Prophet. In the morning they pounced on him; seeing ‘Ali (RA), Allah foiled their plot. They said, where is that companion of yours? He said, I do not know.{{3}}
blocks.34: The Prophet {{1}} did not say to anyone, come, let us flee. He left one man lying in the bed. And that ‘one’ lay there without a question.{{2}}
blocks.35: After the council broke up Jibril (AS) came and said to the Prophet {{1}}, tonight do not stay in your usual bed. Night came. The youths gathered at the door, to pounce as soon as the Prophet {{2}} slept. The Prophet {{3}} said to ‘Ali (RA), wear this green Hadrami cloak of mine and lie in my bed; no harm from them will reach you. He used to sleep wearing this very cloak.{{4}}
blocks.36: The scene after this has come with a still weaker chain. Ibn Ishaq took it from Muhammad ibn Ka‘b al-Qurazi, a Tabi‘i; in the chain is a narrator named Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, whom the hadith scholars have called weak. So this is only a scene. In the narration, before the people gathered at the door Abu Jahl was saying loudly, Muhammad says, if you follow his path you will be kings of the Arabs and non-Arabs, will be raised after death, will get Paradise; if you do not accept, you will be slaughtered, will be raised after death and burn in fire. Then the Prophet {{1}} came out. A handful of dust in his hand. He said, yes, I say that. And you are one of them. Allah took away their sight. The Prophet {{2}} went on reciting the opening verses of Surah Ya Sin as he scattered dust on their heads. One came and asked, whom are you waiting for here? They said, Muhammad. He said, may Allah thwart you. Muhammad has gone out putting dust on all your heads. Put a hand on your head and see. Each put a hand on his head. Dust. They peeked in and saw someone lying in the bed wrapped in a cloak. They said, there is Muhammad, sleeping. Morning came. From the bed rose ‘Ali (RA).{{3}}
blocks.38: Preparation for the journey was in the house of Abu Bakr (RA).
blocks.40: We prepared provisions for them swiftly, and packed food in a pouch. Asma’ bint Abi Bakr (RA) cut a piece of her waistband and tied the mouth of the pouch with it. For this reason she was named ‘Dhat al-Nitaq’ (the one with the waistband).{{1}}
blocks.41: In the arrangement of this journey everyone had one task.
blocks.43: Then the Messenger of Allah {{1}} and Abu Bakr (RA) reached a cave on Mount Thawr and hid there three nights. ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr (RA) would spend the night with them; he was young, intelligent and sharp. In the last part of the night he would leave them, and in the morning be with Quraysh in Makkah, as if he had spent the night there. If he heard of any plot against them he would remember it, and when the darkness of evening fell he would come to them and tell. ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah (RA), the freed slave of Abu Bakr (RA), would graze a flock of milch goats for them, and after the first watch of the night had passed he would bring it to them. The two of them would spend the night on the milk of those goats and bread baked on hot stones.{{2}}
blocks.46: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} and Abu Bakr (RA) hired a man of the Banu Dil tribe as a guide; he was especially skilled at knowing the way. He was still in the religion of the disbelievers of Quraysh. Considering him trustworthy, they handed him their two mounts and took his promise that after three nights, at morning, he would arrive at the cave of Thawr with the mounts.{{2}}
blocks.47: In this choice the question was not of faith; it was of competence for the task and of trustworthiness. The right man for the right task. No one’s task is big, no one’s task is small; all tasks together make one journey.
blocks.49: Morning came. Makkah woke up. The one they were to catch was not in the bed. ‘Ali (RA) was there. Then the search began. House by house, road by road. A reward was announced. Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) has said, they went on following the footprints.
blocks.51: They followed his footprints. Reaching the mountain the tracks became confused. They climbed the mountain, passed by the front of the cave, saw a spider’s web at its mouth. They said, had anyone entered here, the spider’s web would not be on its mouth. He stayed there three nights.{{1}}
blocks.54: In the cave I said to the Prophet {{1}}, if any of them looks beneath his feet, he will see us. He said, O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two of whom the third is Allah?{{2}}
blocks.55: In one sentence all the fear of the cave was washed away. The Qur’an has kept this event. The disbelievers had driven him out; he was ‘the second of the two’.
blocks.57: If you do not help him (that is, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace), (there is no harm to him in that. For) Allah did help him at that time too, when the disbelievers had driven him out (of Makkah), and he was the second of the two, when the two were in the cave, when he said to his companion, do not grieve, Allah is with us. So Allah sent down tranquillity upon him from Himself and helped him with forces you did not see, and made the word of the disbelievers the lowest. In truth the word of Allah is the highest. Allah is Mighty and Wise.{{1}}
blocks.58: Before the cave were four months of feeding camels, leaving someone in the bed, hiring a guide, having news brought at night. And inside the cave exactly this sentence. Preparation and trust; both together. The question with which today’s dars began, its answer is here.
blocks.60: After three nights he came out of the cave. They took the road, with the guide of Banu Dil, toward Madinah. About the road Abu Bakr (RA) himself has told. The father of al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (RA) was buying a camel-saddle from him; the father said, the saddle will not go until you tell the story of setting out from Makkah.
blocks.62: We set out from Makkah; we travelled the whole night and the whole day. The harsh time of noon came. I looked around to see if there was a little shade to take shelter in. I saw a rock. Going to it I saw that a little shade was there. I levelled the place and spread a bed for the Messenger of Allah {{1}}. I said, lie down, O Prophet of Allah. He lay down. I went out looking around to see whether anyone had followed. I saw a shepherd coming with his sheep toward that rock, wanting what we had wanted. I asked, O boy, whose are you? He named a man of Quraysh, and I recognised him. I said, is there milk in your sheep? He said, there is. I said, will you milk? He said, yes. I said, hold one sheep, brush the udder free of dust, then brush your hands. He struck one hand against the other to show. Then he milked some milk for me. I had a vessel for the Messenger of Allah {{2}}, with cloth wrapped around its mouth. I poured water over the milk so that the bottom cooled. Then I took it to the Prophet {{3}}. I saw that he had woken up. I said, drink, O Messenger of Allah. He drank so that my heart was filled with joy. Then I said, the time to travel has come. He said, yes. We set out.{{4}}
blocks.63: The Prophet {{1}} sleeping. And one man awake, guarding. First water in the vessel of milk, so that the hot milk would cool for the Prophet {{2}}. Another story of another place Abu Bakr (RA) has also told. In one tent, only a woman. She said, I am alone, go to the elders of the tribe. The Prophet {{3}} had set out toward that very tent. The woman’s son brought a thin goat. The Prophet {{4}} stroked its udder and milked; the vessel filled. That woman, then Abu Bakr (RA), then the other goats too; one by one everyone drank. The woman later used to call him ‘al-Mubarak’. Her goats multiplied. Abu Bakr (RA) later recognised that son in Madinah and said, this is the companion of that ‘al-Mubarak’. The woman came and said, take me to him. She went to the Prophet {{5}}, and the Prophet {{6}} gave her something.{{7}}

footnotes.0: The Hijrah of Banu Jahsh and the empty house: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Chapter on the Hijrah from Makkah to Madinah’ (from Ibn Ishaq; a narration of the Sirah, as a scene). The verse ‘Utbah recited, according to Ibn Hisham, is from a poem of Abu Dawud al-Ayadi. At that time ‘Abbas ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib had not believed.
footnotes.1: From ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) (via Nafi‘, Ibn ‘Umar): Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Chapter on the Hijrah from Makkah to Madinah’ (via Ibn Ishaq; a narration of the Sirah, as a scene); also in al-Raheeq al-Makhtum, p. 275
footnotes.3: The background of the Quraysh council: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 1, note 18 on Surah al-Anfal 8:30, p. 496: when the disbelievers of Makkah saw that Islam was spreading fast and that many people in Madinah had accepted Islam, they called a consultative council. Three proposals came there: arrest, killing and exile. The final decision was that they would kill, choosing one youth from each of the various tribes and attacking together.
footnotes.4: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 1, Surah al-Anfal 8:30, p. 496 (translation: Tawdih al-Qur’an)
footnotes.5: Musnad Ahmad 3251 (from Ibn ‘Abbas (RA)); al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar: chain hasan
footnotes.6: The council of Dar al-Nadwah: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Section on the reason for the Hijrah of the Messenger of Allah {{1}} himself’ (Ibn Ishaq ← ‘man la attahimu’ (an unspecified trustworthy person) ← Ibn Abi Najih ← Mujahid ← Ibn ‘Abbas (RA)). In the chain Ibn Ishaq did not disclose one person’s name; Ibn Kathir has said that al-Waqidi too has brought a similar account via ‘A’ishah, Ibn ‘Abbas, ‘Ali and Suraqah. A narration of the Sirah, as a scene; no creed or evidence has been built upon it.
footnotes.7: The Prophet’s {{1}} coming to the house of Abu Bakr (RA) every morning and evening: Sahih al-Bukhari 3905 (from ‘A’ishah (RA); the opening part of the hadith: ‘lam yamurra ‘alayna yawmun illa yatina fihi Rasulullahi {{2}} tarafayin nahari bukratan wa ‘ashiyyah’).
footnotes.10: Musnad Ahmad 3251 (from Ibn ‘Abbas (RA)); al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar: chain hasan
footnotes.11: The matter of surrounding the house: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 1, note 18 on Surah al-Anfal 8:30, p. 496 (the enemies had besieged his house); in Musnad Ahmad 3251 too there is the polytheists’ guarding of ‘Ali (RA).
footnotes.12: Jibril’s warning and ‘Ali’s cloak: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Section on the reason for the Hijrah of the Messenger of Allah {{1}}’ (Ibn Ishaq ← the chain of Ibn ‘Abbas, the same narration mentioned for the Dar al-Nadwah council, an unspecified narrator in the chain); a narration of the Sirah, as a scene.
footnotes.13: The narration of scattering dust and reciting Ya Sin: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Section on the reason for the Hijrah of the Messenger of Allah {{1}}’ (Ibn Ishaq ← Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad ← Muhammad ibn Ka‘b al-Qurazi). Mursal (from a Tabi‘i) and a weak narrator in the chain; weak level; as a scene, not as evidence. The basic foundation of the event’s truth: the Qur’an 8:30 and Ahmad 3251 (‘Ali in the bed and the polytheists’ guarding).
footnotes.17: Musnad Ahmad 3251 (from Ibn ‘Abbas (RA)); al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar: chain hasan
footnotes.18: Sahih al-Bukhari 3653 (from Abu Bakr (RA)); to the same effect, Sahih al-Bukhari 4663
footnotes.19: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 1, Surah al-Tawbah 9:40, pp. 539–540 (translation: Tawdih al-Qur’an)
footnotes.20: Sahih al-Bukhari 3652 (from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (RA), the narration from Abu Bakr’s (RA) mouth)
footnotes.21: The story of the woman in the tent and the goat: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Story of Umm Ma‘bad al-Khuza‘iyyah’ (al-Bayhaqi, ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla ← Abu Bakr (RA)); Ibn Kathir: ‘chain hasan’. Al-Bayhaqi wrote that this story is like the story of Umm Ma‘bad, perhaps the very same. The detailed description (hulyah) of Umm Ma‘bad and the poem of the jinn have come with a different chain; left out because they were not verified in this dars. The incident of Umm Ma‘bad is in al-Raheeq al-Makhtum on p. 292.

quiz.q: What did ‘Utbah do on seeing the empty house of Banu Jahsh?
o: Sighed and said, every house is seized by calamity one day
Blamed the Prophet ﷺ like Abu Jahl, then spoke to ‘Abbas
Took the house with ‘Abbas, then locked it
Sent men to bring back ‘Abdullah ibn Jahsh (RA), then went back

quiz.q: What did ‘Umar (RA) offer ‘Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi‘ah (RA) so that he would not go?
o: His own she-camel, which he gave at the time of going
Security of staying at Quba, which was for Abu Salamah (RA)
A pact with Abu Jahl, which never happened
Half of his own wealth

quiz.q: For how long did Abu Bakr (RA), hoping to be the Prophet’s ﷺ companion, feed his two mounts samur leaves?
o: Three nights, as long as they had to stay in the cave
Fourteen nights, as long as he stayed at Quba
Ten years, as long as he was called season after season
Four months

quiz.q: Why did the Prophet ﷺ not go before the permission for Hijrah came?
o: He did not want to leave Makkah, so he sent his companions first
Abu Bakr’s (RA) mounts were not ready, so there was delay
The Ansar had not yet pledged, so he waited
He was waiting for Allah’s permission; the companions went first
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 3905: ‘I hope I will be given permission’.

quiz.q: What is the last word of verse 8:30 about the night council of Quraysh?
o: They were plotting; Allah was also planning, He is the best of planners
Do not grieve, Allah is with us, which was said in the cave
The word of Allah is uppermost; Allah is Mighty and Wise, the words of 9:40
Allah sent down tranquillity upon him and sent unseen forces
quiz.e: Surah al-Anfal 8:30; the other three are the words of Surah al-Tawbah 9:40.

quiz.q: What was the main feature of the arrangement of the journey to the cave of Thawr?
o: Everyone staying together in the cave
Fixing one person for each task
Leaving it to supplication alone, with no preparation
Taking all help from the polytheists

quiz.q: The guide was a polytheist; why did the Prophet ﷺ still hire him?
o: He had secretly accepted Islam, so the Prophet ﷺ trusted him
Quraysh did not want to catch him, so it seemed safe
Because he was skilled at knowing the way and trustworthy
He was a relative of Abu Bakr (RA), so he was trusted

quiz.q: At work you have been given the responsibility of a task, one step of which you will give to another trustworthy person. Which scene matches?
o: Giving the guide’s task to one who was trustworthy and skilled
Giving someone responsibility because he is a relative of Abu Bakr (RA)
Keeping all the work in your own hands and trusting no one
Not letting any outsider into any step, out of fear

quiz.q: You work in an organisation where everyone thinks their own work small. In the light of the journey to the cave of Thawr, what would you say?
o: Counting only the work of the one who goes first as real
No one’s work is small; all work together makes a journey
Moving on, leaving out the one who is afraid
Who was in the cave is the greatest matter, the rest are secondary
quiz.e: ‘Ali (RA), Asma’ (RA), ‘Abdullah, ‘Amir, the guide; the role of all.

quiz.q: Seeing the spider’s web at the mouth of the cave, what did Quraysh decide?
o: Set fire to the cave so that whoever was inside would come out
Called Abu Bakr (RA) to find who was inside
Split into groups and spread out in all directions to search
Had anyone entered, the web would not have been there; so they moved away

quiz.q: Who said to whom in the cave of Thawr, ‘What do you think of two of whom the third is Allah’?
o: The Prophet ﷺ to Abu Bakr (RA)
Abu Bakr (RA) to the Prophet ﷺ
‘Ali (RA) to the Prophet ﷺ
‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr (RA) to Abu Bakr (RA)

quiz.q: In Sahih al-Bukhari 3652, what did Abu Bakr (RA) do on the road at noon?
o: Spread a bed in the shade of a rock, brought milk
Asked Suraqah for a paper of security, when he was on his horse
Seeing the spider’s web at the cave’s mouth, moved away
Cut a waistband and tied the mouth of the pouch
